title: How Long Does It Take to Build a Website in Hong Kong?
description: Realistic timelines for building a website in Hong Kong — from a two-week landing page to a three-month custom build — and what actually slows a project down.

content.text: Timelines depend on the type of site

A website project in Hong Kong can take anywhere from two weeks to three months or more. The fastest projects are simple landing pages; the longest are custom builds with back-end systems and integrations.
Typical timeframes

items: Landing page or brochure site: 2 to 4 weeks
Standard business website with a content management system: 4 to 8 weeks
eCommerce site with payments and shipping: 6 to 12 weeks
Custom web application or portal: 3 months and up

content.text: What slows projects down

Most delays are not caused by the developers. Content that arrives late, decisions that wait on a committee, feedback cycles that run for days, and scope added mid-build are the usual culprits. The more prepared your content and decisions are, the faster the build goes.
How to keep the timeline honest

Agree on a milestone plan up front and treat the dates seriously. Ask what the developer does when a milestone slips, and be clear about what you are responsible for providing. A realistic schedule with a responsible partner beats a fast promise that quietly slips for months. For a realistic timeline on your project, talk to we2Tech for a free consultation.

title: 7 Signs Your Business Website Needs a Redesign
description: Is your website costing you customers? These seven warning signs show when it is time to redesign your Hong Kong business website.

content.text: Your website is working against you
A website does not need to be broken to be a problem. It can quietly lose you customers every day, and the warning signs are usually easy to spot once you know what to look for.
Seven warning signs

items: Your bounce rate is high and visitors leave within seconds
The site looks dated or does not reflect your current branding
It does not work well on phones, which is where most Hong Kong traffic comes from
Pages take several seconds to load
You cannot update content yourself and every change costs money
Google shows competitors above you and your traffic has stalled
The site does not capture leads or sales the way it used to

content.text: Why waiting is expensive
Every month you keep an underperforming site is a month of missed enquiries. A modern site that loads fast and works on mobile is no longer a luxury, it is the minimum standard customers expect.
What a redesign should fix

A good redesign starts with your business goals, not just a new look. It should improve speed, mobile experience, clarity of message and how visitors turn into enquiries. If several of the signs above apply to you, it is worth a conversation about a redesign with the we2Tech team.

title: How Much Does an eCommerce Website Cost in Hong Kong?
description: What an online shop really costs to build in Hong Kong in 2026 — platforms, custom builds, payment gateways and the hidden costs most quotes leave out.

content.text: What an online shop really costs

An online shop in Hong Kong can cost anywhere from a few thousand to several hundred thousand Hong Kong dollars. The difference comes down to what you need to sell, take payments and manage stock, not the size of the shopfront.
Three common ways to build
Most Hong Kong businesses start with one of three approaches, and each has a very different price band.

items: Template setup on Shopify or WooCommerce: roughly HKD 15,000 to 60,000, including theme, payments and shipping setup
Custom storefront: roughly HKD 80,000 to 250,000 for a build tailored to your brand and checkout flow
Complex builds with ERP or inventory integrations: HKD 250,000 and up, depending on how many systems must talk to each other

content.text: What actually drives the price

The number of products, the payment methods you accept, shipping rules and languages all change the workload. Supporting PayMe, AlipayHK and Octopus alongside cards adds real integration work, and a bilingual English and Traditional Chinese storefront roughly doubles the content and testing effort.
The hidden costs

Domain names, SSL certificates, payment gateway fees, hosting and monthly maintenance are rarely included in the initial build price. Cheap one-off builds often look affordable until these recurring costs and change requests arrive later.
Budget with the outcome in mind

Start from what you want the shop to achieve, not from a feature list. An itemised quote with milestones and clear deliverables protects you from scope creep and keeps the budget predictable. title: What to Look for in a Web Development Proposal
description: How to read a web development proposal so you can compare quotes fairly, spot missing scope and pick a partner who will actually deliver.

content.text: Proposals are not all the same
Two proposals for the same website can look nothing alike, and price alone tells you very little. The value is in the detail of what is included, what is excluded and how the work is phased.
What a good proposal must contain

items: A clear scope with pages and features listed, not vague phrases like "modern design"
Milestones with dates and a payment schedule tied to completion, not just a start and end date
What happens on change requests, because scope changes are when cost overruns happen
Hosting, domain, SSL and maintenance made explicit so there are no surprises later
Who does the work, including whether design and development are in-house or subcontracted

content.text: Red flags to watch for

Be wary of proposals with no milestones, fixed prices with no mention of changes, or quotes that are dramatically lower than everything else. A price that looks too good usually means scope that will expand later.
Compare on process, not just price

The best way to compare is to ask each vendor the same questions and lay the proposals side by side. Look for the one that understands your business problem, not just the one that lists the most features. The we2Tech team will happily walk you through a detailed proposal so you know exactly what you are paying for.

title: How Much Does a Mobile App Cost in Hong Kong in 2026?
description: A realistic guide to mobile app development costs in Hong Kong in 2026. See what drives the price and what a typical MVP, mid-range and enterprise app really costs.

content.text: "How much does an app cost?" is the first question every business asks. The honest answer is that it depends on scope — but you can plan with realistic figures if you understand what drives the price.
The short answer

In Hong Kong in 2026, a production-ready app typically falls into one of three bands. An MVP with a focused feature set starts around HKD 150,000–300,000. A mid-range app with custom design, user accounts and payment integration is typically HKD 300,000–800,000. A complex enterprise app — logistics, finance, multi-role operations — can run from HKD 800,000 upwards.
What drives the cost

items: Platforms: iOS only, Android only, or both. Cross-platform frameworks like React Native or Flutter keep one codebase for both, lowering cost.
Features: the more screens, roles, integrations and data flows, the more design and engineering hours.
Design: custom UI/UX design costs more than template-based work — and is usually worth it.
Backend and cloud: accounts, payments, dashboards and APIs all add significant work.
Ongoing support: maintenance, hosting, monitoring and updates are a separate monthly or yearly cost.

content.text: Why Hong Kong rates vary

Rates in Hong Kong sit higher than in many offshore markets because of local hiring costs, higher English and Cantonese fluency, and the expectation of close collaboration. In return you get shorter feedback loops and a team you can meet face-to-face.
How to get an accurate quote

The fastest way to a realistic budget is to share your business goal, target users, current workflow and any systems you already use. A good team will turn that into a fixed-scope quotation with milestones — not an open-ended hourly estimate.

title: React Native vs Flutter: Which Should You Choose?
description: React Native and Flutter are the two leading cross-platform frameworks in 2026. We compare performance, developer experience, ecosystem and cost to help you decide.

content.text: If you want one codebase for iOS and Android, React Native and Flutter are the two realistic options in 2026. Both are mature, but they suit different teams and different projects.
React Native

React Native renders native components through JavaScript and React. Its biggest advantage is the JavaScript ecosystem: if you already use React on the web, you can share logic and even whole modules between your web app and mobile app. It has the largest talent pool, extensive libraries, and over-the-air updates that many teams rely on.
Flutter

Flutter draws its own UI with a high-performance engine, which gives exceptionally consistent look-and-feel across platforms. Teams often cite smoother animations, strong developer tooling and excellent widget catalogues. It is a great choice when pixel-perfect custom UI matters more than sharing code with an existing React web app.
How to choose

items: Choose React Native if you have (or want) a React web app and want to share code and talent.
Choose Flutter if you want the most consistent custom UI with top-tier animation performance.
If you are starting from scratch with a small team, your own team’s language skills often decide it — there is no wrong answer for most business apps.
For heavy native features, sensor work or deep OS integration, evaluate native iOS/Android alongside the cross-platform option.

title: How Much Does a Website Cost in Hong Kong in 2026?
description: Website pricing in Hong Kong explained: brochure sites, corporate websites and web applications. What you pay for and how to budget in 2026.

content.text: Website costs in Hong Kong range from a few thousand dollars for a template site to seven figures for a full web platform. The difference is scope — and what you actually need to achieve.
Typical price bands

items: Template/brochure site: HKD 8,000–30,000. Pre-built design, a handful of pages, simple content updates.
Custom corporate website: HKD 40,000–120,000. Custom design, CMS, SEO-ready structure, multilingual support.
Web application (portal, dashboard, eCommerce): HKD 150,000+. Login, payments, data, integrations and ongoing development.

content.text: What you are paying for

Beyond the visible pages you are paying for information architecture, responsive design, SEO fundamentals, speed, security, and a CMS your team can actually use. Cheap sites cut exactly these corners — and you feel it in search rankings and bounce rate.
Cheap vs right-sized

A low-cost site can be a fine first step, but many businesses rebuild within two years because the cheap version caps their growth. A right-sized site, built on solid foundations, earns its cost back through enquiries and brand credibility.
Budgeting tips

items: Start with the outcome: do you need leads, online bookings, or a full product?
Plan for 3–5 core pages done well rather than 30 pages done poorly.
Budget separately for copywriting, photography and ongoing SEO.
Include maintenance: hosting, updates, backups and small edits.

title: Mobile App vs Web App: Which Do You Need?
description: App or website? We break down the real differences between mobile apps and web apps — reach, cost, UX and offline — so you can decide with confidence.

content.text: Clients often ask whether they need a mobile app or a web application. The right answer depends on how your users will engage, not on which option is trendier.
Choose a mobile app when

items: Users need it on the go — in the field, in a warehouse, on public transport.
You want push notifications to re-engage users.
You need offline capability or deep device features like camera, GPS or sensors.
You are building a consumer product where app-store presence matters.

content.text: Choose a web app when

items: Your users are mostly on desktop or laptop browsers.
You need to update content quickly without app-store review cycles.
Budget is tighter and time-to-market matters more.
You want one version that works on any device with no installation.

content.text: The hybrid reality
Many projects are really a web app plus a thin mobile wrapper, or a mobile app with a web dashboard for staff. Defining the split early saves months and budget.
Making the decision

Map your primary user journeys, your team’s ability to maintain updates, and your growth stage. A consultation to clarify feasibility and risk before a full project is confirmed is exactly what we are here for — and it is free.

title: How to Choose a Software Development Company in Hong Kong
description: 10 questions to ask before hiring an app or web development company in Hong Kong. A practical checklist to avoid expensive mistakes.

content.text: The success of your project depends less on the tech stack and more on who you hire. Here is the checklist we would use ourselves.
The checklist

items: Do they ask about your business before talking features? Watch for teams that sell screens instead of outcomes.
Can they show relevant work — and explain what they would do differently now?
Who does the work? Ask whether it is in-house, outsourced, or subcontracted.
How do they handle scope changes? Fixed-price vendors are not all equal.
What is the testing and launch process? QA is where most budgets blow up.
Do they offer support after launch? A project without maintenance is a liability.
Can they speak your language — literally and technically?
What happens to your code and data if you part ways?
Is there a clear communication cadence and a named project contact?
Will they tell you when you do not need them? The best advice is sometimes “don’t build this yet”.

content.text: Red flags
Avoid teams that guarantee impossible timelines, refuse to discuss ownership, outsource silently, or quote a fixed price before understanding the scope. These lead to the most common horror stories.
